🌕 Still over the moon after the eclipse?

Keep exploring space at the Science Museum this summer. 

See a real piece of the Moon, join our free daily Space on a Sphere shows, enjoy a family Space Show or follow our free space lovers' trail: https://bit.ly/4hxwksu

🎬 The adventure isn't over yet…

New screenings of The Odyssey in magnificent IMAX 70mm are now on sale. 

Experience it on the big screen - book your tickets now: https://bit.ly/4w4CZhf

#TheOdyssey #IMAX70mm #ScienceMuseum

© 2025 UNIVERSAL STUDIOS

🎉Happy International Day of Friendship!  

Round up your favourite people and take on the world of gaming at Power Up. From Pac-Man to Mario, there's something for every player.  

Book your tickets now: https://bit.ly/4yPFk2c

#ScienceMuseum #GamingExperience #FunDayOut

Immerse yourself in the world of bubbles with Bubble Explorers family show at the Science Museum – exciting experiments, moments of wow and a chance to practice your scientific exploration skills. 🫧  

Don't miss it – book now: https://bit.ly/3TrVU8i

#ScienceMuseum #ThingsToDoInLondon #FamilyDayOut

🚨  We've got great news...  

New additional screenings to watch and experience The Odyssey in glorious IMAX 70 mm are now on sale. 

Don't miss it – book now: https://bit.ly/4pDvyME

#TheOdyssey #IMAX70mm #ScienceMuseum

Today, it’s Ice Cream Day. Celebrate the sweetest day of the year with a trip to Wonderlab for hands-on, mind-blowing family fun, then top it off with a scoop of your favourite ice cream or shake at the Shake Bar.

Book now: https://bit.ly/4eXdeuc

Tonight, England face Argentina in a massive World Cup semi-final. But the tournament would look very different without the science behind its kits, ball and trophy. 

Explore the chemical history of three crucial ‘elements’ of the World Cup in this blog from our archives: https://bit.ly/4ykDNkr

Calling all teachers ⚗️🧮

Join our fully funded CPD courses next term at the Science Museum.

From exploring science through play to setting up your own STEM skills club, our courses are specially designed for educators by the Science Museum Group Academy.

Book here: https://bit.ly/4f2UR5X

As seen on Bargain Hunt today: step inside the Science and Innovation Park and discover what happens behind the scenes at the Hawking Building, where over 300,000 objects from the UK's national science collection are cared for.

Watch the 5-minute film: https://bbc.in/4gXFLB9

Ahead of our upcoming exhibition Becoming America: how science shaped a nation, supported by Griffin Catalyst, our latest blog post explores the scientific thinking that underpinned the Declaration of Independence: https://bit.ly/4eKhgGk

As we celebrate 50 years of partnership between the Science Museum and @wellcometrust.bsky.social this month, Keeper of Medicine Katie Dabin explores the fascinating medicine collection we care for – plus some of our curators’ favourite objects – in a new blog: https://bit.ly/4oTTk6N

We are thrilled that His Majesty The King received a Fellowship of the Science Museum Group yesterday at Buckingham Palace, presented by our Chair of Trustees Sir Tim Laurence and Director Sir Ian Blatchford. 

Find out more here: https://bit.ly/4oV1FHd

In our latest #ObjectSpotlight video, Curator Stewart Emmens reveals the hidden details of an eye-catching miniature hospital — one which had royal support and an important social role in the days before the NHS. 

Visit Medicine: The Wellcome Galleries: https://bit.ly/4eh93ZY

Tickets for The Odyssey are finally on sale!

This summer's most anticipated epic is finally here – in a world-first feature shot entirely with IMAX cameras, watch The Odyssey the way Christoper Nolan intended in our breathtaking IMAX 70mm cinema at the Science Museum.

Book now: bit.ly/4uv7MTK

We're happy to announce that the Science Museum has been shortlisted in the Best Venue for STEM Learning category at this year’s School Travel Awards!

If you've joined us on a school visit to the museum recently, we would be grateful if you could support us via this link: https://bit.ly/4vMwujN

Today may be #WorldDraculaDay, but don't worry, our galleries, including Medicine: The Wellcome Galleries, where you can explore microscopic slides from blood cells and learn about the quest to better understand the human body, are open daily, 10.00–18.00.

🚨 It’s your last chance to see Water Pantanal Fire — our thought-provoking photography exhibition closes on Sunday 31 May. 

Don’t miss this ‘breathtaking, sobering exhibition’ (Secret London), full of striking images from the Pantanal wetland. 

Book free tickets: https://bit.ly/498VxVd

This International Museum Day, we’re celebrating the people who make it all possible, working before the doors open at the Science Museum.

From cleaners and conservators to technicians, front-of-house staff, and security, mornings at the museum are a team effort.

We’re ready https://bit.ly/3IfVqd7

To celebrate #JewishCultureMonth, you can follow this self-led trail which explores how people from diverse Jewish backgrounds have pioneered medical innovations that transformed health and medicine today: https://bit.ly/492BXda

📷 Pohl Omniskop X-ray apparatus, c.1925-1935 with control panel unit

On this day in 1796, Edward Jenner carried out the world’s first vaccination – injecting a boy with cowpox to protect him from the deadly smallpox.

Even the word “vaccine” comes from the Latin word for cow: vacca. 🐄

Discover more about Jenner here 👉 https://bit.ly/3Bupei3
